messages:
alex: FYI I found a noisy debug line in canary logs that contains a session cookie fragment. Not sure if full tokens were logged, need quick scope + comms guidance. /cc @camila @tariq :warning:
camila: oncall here, can you paste the exact log line and the service? I can gate canary if this is high-risk.
alex: service=ingest-canary, host=canary-7, here's the snippet (redacted context):
```
2025-11-03T14:12:03Z DEBUG user=123 action="auth" details="session=eyJhbGciOiJIU...XYZ partial"
```
alex: only a partial JWT-looking string, not full header. Appears from a debug wrapper in oauth client during retry path.
tariq: :eyes: do we have evidence the JWT was accepted by any upstream? Any requests showing auth success with that cookie?
alex: checked upstream logs -> no matching auth success with that token fragment. Also TTL suggests rotated within 5m window; user session still valid but not correlated to this fragment.
camila: ok sounds contained, but we should treat as potential exposure. Steps: 1) rotate affected session keys, 2) remove debug logging path, 3) determine who pulled the logs (S3/staging). I'll kick off the rotation now.
camila: @tariq can you confirm whether this meets incident-reporting threshold for privacy team and whether we need customer comms?
tariq: quick read: scope looks limited to staging canary host and debug-level logs. If the fragment can't be used to replay auth (no matching header) I would classify as a low-severity privacy incident, but we should still file a P2 incident for tracking and run a short audit on log access.
camila: noted. Alex, can you revert the debug flag and push the fix to canary? If yes, reply with the deploy link.
alex: pushed a revert PR and disabled debug wrapper on canary-7. Deploy link: https://ci.internal/redwood/ingest/3872 — deploy started.
oncall-bot: Deploy started by alex on ingest-canary (build 3872).
camila: good. @elena from comms/legal — do we need external notification or this stays internal?
elena: from a legal POV, if token material was present somewhere publicly accessible (S3 bucket, shared logs) we escalate. If this stayed in staging and only internal S3 access, no customer comms. Please confirm storage path and ACLs.
tariq: I ran a quick S3 ACL check: logs are in s3://redwood-stage-logs/canary/2025-11-03 and ACL is restricted to internal roles. I'll attach the audit in the incident ticket. (reacted :white_check_mark:)
alex: added audit link: https://internal.ticket/INC-2025-911 (private) — includes who accessed the object in last 72h.
camila: thanks. Elena, based on that, any further asks?
elena: if access is internal only and we rotated sessions, we don't need customer comms. Document timeline and approvals in the ticket and mark as P2. Also please add a short postmortem entry for logging guidelines.
tariq: I'll add a follow-up task: scan codebase for other debug wrappers that log auth tokens and create a lint rule.
camila: agreed. Alex — please include the exact grep pattern you used to find the line in the ticket so devs can search.
alex: added grep: `grep -R "session=[A-Za-z0-9._-]\{20,\}" ./logs` to the ticket.
camila: closing on slack for now — we'll continue async in INC-2025-911. Thanks all. :lock:
